Maternity leave in the UAE private sector

LeaveLengthPay
Maternity leave60 days45 days full pay, 15 days half pay
Pregnancy or delivery illnessUp to 45 more daysUnpaid, not counted as service
Sick or disabled baby30 days, extendable by 30Full pay, then unpaid
Parental leave (either parent)5 working days within 6 monthsFull pay
Nursing breaksUp to 1 hour a day for 6 monthsPaid

Example: basic salary AED 6,000 and allowances AED 3,000 (gross AED 9,000).

Daily wage = 9,000 ÷ 30 = AED 300.
45 days on full pay = AED 13,500. 15 days on half pay = AED 2,250.
Maternity pay = AED 15,750 for 60 days, against AED 18,000 of normal pay.

Some employers calculate maternity pay on basic salary only. The law says "full pay" and defines pay as including allowances, so the calculator uses gross pay by default and lets you switch. Prefer Arabic? Use the Arabic version.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a minimum period of service for maternity leave?

No. The current text of Article 30 gives 60 days of maternity leave with no service requirement: 45 days on full pay and 15 days on half pay.

When can maternity leave start?

It may start from the last day of the month before the expected month of delivery, at the employee's request and with a medical certificate giving the likely date.

Am I entitled to leave if the baby is stillborn?

Yes. Maternity leave is due if delivery happens after six months or more of pregnancy, even if the baby is stillborn or dies after birth.

What is parental leave in the UAE?

Five paid working days for the father or the mother, taken in one block or separately within six months of the birth, on proof of birth. It is separate from maternity leave.

Do I get nursing breaks after I return?

Yes. One or two breaks a day totalling no more than one hour, for six months from the delivery date. The UAE Government portal says they are paid.

Do the extra pregnancy-illness days count as service?

No. The additional absence of up to 45 unpaid days for illness caused by pregnancy or delivery is not counted as service for end-of-service gratuity or pension.

I heard about 90 days in Abu Dhabi — does it apply to me?

In 2024 Abu Dhabi announced a programme giving Emirati women in the emirate's private sector 90 days of maternity leave. It is optional for employers and not part of federal law. The federal minimum for all employees is still 60 days.

  • Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021 and its amendments — MOHRE consolidated text (Articles 30 and 32)
